title: She didn’t recognize Jesus.
paragraphs: She didn’t recognize Jesus.
Not until He said her name.
“Mary.” — John 20:16
That is the moment that breaks me every time.

Mary Magdalene came to the tomb carrying grief like a wound that would not close. She was weeping outside the place where death had made its claim. The stone was moved. The body was gone. Heaven had already shifted history, but her heart was still trapped in Friday.
And that is how many of us live.

Jesus is risen.
But we are still crying at tombs.

Still staring at what we lost.
Still reaching for what we cannot fix.
Still assuming the worst when God has already begun the miracle.
Then Jesus speaks one word.
Her name.

Not a lecture.
Not a rebuke.
Not a cold correction.
Just “Mary.”

And in that single word, darkness cracked.
Confusion fell apart.
Love became recognizable.
Brother, sister, hear me.

The risen Christ does not only conquer the grave in public power. He meets broken people in personal tenderness. Mary had a past. Mary had known bondage. Mary had known deliverance. And now at the tomb, she learns this: the same Jesus who cast out her darkness is the Jesus who walked out of death itself.
That is the Gospel.

Our sin is real.
Our sorrow is deep.
Our blindness is stubborn.
But Jesus is alive.

He died for sinners.
He rose again in victory.
And He still calls people by name—out of shame, out of despair, out of dead places, into repentance, into mercy, into new life.
Mary thought the story ended at the tomb.
But grace was standing right in front of her.

And maybe that is where you are today.
Crying.
Confused.
Wounded.
Looking at an empty place and calling it the end.
But here’s what we miss: when Jesus calls your name, the grave no longer gets the last word.

So turn.
Like Mary turned.

Turn from unbelief.
Turn from hidden sin.
Turn from the voices that keep you chained to yesterday.
And answer the living Christ.
Because the Savior who called “Mary” is still calling hearts today.
And His voice still brings dead things back to life.
Hope is not buried. Jesus is risen.
